answer: A place with truly beautiful views that I will never forget was the top of a hill in Bandarban, in the Chittagong Hill Tracts, which I hiked up during a trip with friends about three years ago. We travelled by bus to Bandarban town, then took a jeep along winding mountain roads to a small village, and from there we climbed on foot for about three hours with a local guide. The climb was fairly demanding, especially in the heat, but the reward at the summit was more than worth the effort. The final stretch was so steep that we had to use our hands in places, and I was drenched in sweat by the time we reached the top. From the summit, the view was absolutely [[panoramic]], stretching across valleys, forests and the Sangu river winding through the landscape far below. Layer after layer of green hills faded into the blue distance, and clouds were drifting past almost at eye level. I remember feeling a genuine sense of [[elation]] as I caught my breath and took it all in. The scale of the scenery was [[humbling]], making me feel wonderfully small against such a vast backdrop. We stayed up there for nearly an hour, simply admiring the view, sharing some biscuits and taking photographs. There is something special about a view you have earned through effort, which makes it feel [[all the more rewarding]]. Honestly, it was one of those rare moments when the natural world [[takes your breath away]]. I still picture that view whenever I need a moment of calm.

followUps.answer: Yes, although I do not get many chances, because there are no hills near Sirajganj. When I travel, though, I always try to include a walk or a hike, because it is the best way to see a place properly.

followUps.q: Did you take a lot of photos there?
followUps.answer: Plenty, but none of them really did the view justice. Nowadays I try to take a few photos and then put my phone away, so I can actually enjoy the moment.
